summary:
Round 2 passes for the exact commit 92c07ce0570d7b1a8dfda8c4f0421fd347907833. All four round-1 findings are resolved, each checked on its own evidence. No regressions turned up in the reviewed launch, audit, prepare, report or affinity paths.

SCALE-001 (fixed): the per-rank CPU count is now even at every step size. In campaign.py:26, --cpus-per-task=2*(64//tasks) gives 20, 12, 8 and 6 CPUs per rank at 6, 10, 14 and 18 ranks. That needs 60, 60, 56 and 54 whole cores, never more than the node's 64. The 18-rank step needs exactly the 54 cores used at four GPUs (16 BDs × 3 + 2 helpers × 3). test_scaling.py:93 now checks the physical limit directly (even count, rounded-up cores ≤ 64, at least 54 cores) instead of repeating the formula. Two runtime guards remain: the campaign intersects the CPU masks probed at all step sizes (campaign.py:81) and requires enough complete two-thread cores (support.py:67,72); and each rank checks that its chosen CPUs sit inside its own step's mask (support.py:81). So if Slurm lays steps out differently, the run fails safely; it does not oversubscribe cores. Leaving out --whole is justified by the recorded local srun help.

SCALE-002 (accepted documented risk): README.md:134-141 now states that the 33 batches over 16 BDs average about 2.06 per BD and that this is not a guaranteed minimum. An idle BD aborts the pilot safely, with no retry and no relaxed coverage. This is the documentation option offered in round 1. I am not inferring any minimum batch count per BD.

SCALE-003 (fixed): test_handoff.py builds complete pilot (6-case) and screen (12-case) attempts using the real schedule. They have 15 and 21 numbered Slurm steps, different CPU masks per step size (60/60/56/54 cores), raw receipt hashes, recomputed read-range hashes, native-test receipts, memory receipts and pinned external provenance. Only load_inputs and verify_payloads are mocked; audit(), validate_plan in screen mode, report() and affinity() run unmocked. Each block uses a different base rate, so the exact checks that speedup equals the GPU count and efficiency is 1 would catch rows paired with the wrong block. Corruption tests cover a missing step, a wrong NodeList, a tampered probe, a changed memory receipt, a wrong native-test device, a wrong pilot audit hash and a swapped baseline. The runtime affinity test uses synthetic topology files and rejects SMT siblings shared across ranks. evidence/offline-round02.txt records 16 tests passing in 9.593 s; this is the coordinator's run, not the historical 12-test log.

SCALE-004 (fixed): README.md:40-42 now names the single SMD0 and EB helpers as possible serial bottlenecks. It states that throughput alone cannot attribute a plateau to any cause and that per-rank CPU use is not measured.

Reads denied in round 1 are now resolved inside the checkout. native-unit.json has exit code 0, 1023 test calls and no failed or skipped results, and its SHA is recorded in checks.json. The installed gpu_placement source and its pin are included under evidence/. GPU tests, the compute-node NIC check, the pilot and any speedup remain pending by design. Two low, non-blocking housekeeping items remain (stale metadata in status.json and prepare-smoke.json).

Slurm settings (CR_CORE_MEMORY, no --whole) are taken from the coordinator's record in checks.json; I could not inspect scontrol or srun output.

GPU tests, compute-node NIC counter access, pixel witnesses, the MPI pilot and all performance results remain pending by design and are not verified.

findings.evidence: Resolved. --cpus-per-task=2*(64//tasks) gives an even 20/12/8/6, which needs 60/60/56/54 whole cores (≤ 64; the 54 cores needed at four GPUs fit). test_scaling.py:93 checks the physical limit directly. A mismatched step layout is caught at runtime by the mask intersection (campaign.py:81), the complete-core requirement (support.py:67,72) and the per-rank subset-of-step-mask check (support.py:81).
findings.requested_change: None required. Optionally record the per-step masks from the pilot in its results, to confirm the layout assumption on real hardware.

findings.evidence: Resolved as an accepted, documented risk (the option offered in round 1). It states about 2.06 batches per BD on average, not a minimum. An idle BD aborts safely with no retry, and the coverage requirement in audit.py:24 is not relaxed.
